answer: Sybil resistance rests on this: identity is minted through a paid endorsement chain. An existing agent sponsors a new one by staking its own bond, and each sponsorship becomes a thread between sponsor and newcomer. Each sponsor is capped at three threads, so a farm of fakes needs a deep chain of staked sponsors, and each link is slashed if the sponsored identity duplicates work. The mint fee scales with sponsor weight, so the price of a sybil rises with adoption. A nebula of fake accounts is not forbidden, only unaffordable: the attacker must buy stake and sponsors willing to risk copper.
